title: INT8 calibration sweeper and runtime grace-periods for activation-aware profiles
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight calibration sweeper service and runtime 'grace-period' mechanism to safely deploy activation-aware INT8 profiles (SmoothQuant-style) across mixed traffic models. This ticket covers the orchestration, metrics gating, and kernel-compatibility heuristics required to ship conservative autotuned profiles with automated rollback/fallback behavior.

Background: We already have per-workload calibration and kernel selectors (see dependencies). However, during rollouts some models show intermittent degradation when KV-cache heavy or with long-prefix token distributions. Operators need an automated way to sweep candidate quant profiles over representative slices, detect regression windows, and apply a runtime grace-period so kernels can complete warmup paths before strict latency SLOs are enforced.

Scope:
- Calibration sweeper: a batch/stream job that takes candidate INT8 profiles, runs them across target model shards and corpus slices, and emits a per-profile scorecard (latency p95, per-token quality delta, memory, kernel compatibility flags).
- Runtime grace-periods: a config layer in the serving runtime to accept a 'grace_seconds' and 'warmup_tokens' per rollout step. During grace, requests are served with fallback policy enabled and additional logging/telemetry. After grace, acceptance gates are evaluated before promoting the profile.
- Kernel compatibility heuristics: mapping between profile properties (per-channel scales, layer-skipping flags) and kernel/path choices. If a profile triggers a less-optimal kernel (or unsupported fused op), mark for manual review or extended grace.
- Telemetry and gating: define score thresholds and alerts. Sweeper emits traces and diff metrics against golden baseline. Automatic canary pass if quality delta < 0.5% and p95 latency regression < 10ms for 95% of slices.

Acceptance criteria: all must be satisfied before merging runtime config: 
1) Sweeper produces repeatable scorecards for 10 models across at least 3 different traffic slice distributions.
2) Runtime applies grace-periods and honors fallback policy (traceable through logs).
3) Automatic promotion route works and includes a rollback trigger on quality/latency violation.
4) End-to-end CI tests (unit + e2e) exercising fallback, warmup, and kernel-selection are added.

Technical approach:
- Implement the sweeper as a lightweight job in infra-runner (k8s CronJob prototype) that loads quant profiles from the calibration store, schedules small inference runs on a reserved pool of VMs/GPU nodes, and records metrics to metrics-store.
- The sweeper will run synthetic traffic with trimmed corpora to emulate KV-cache cold/warm states; it will run both short (32-token) and long (1024-token) sequences to capture runtime kernel behavior.
- Runtime: add 'grace_period' and 'warmup_tokens' fields to rollout policy; implement a multi-state route (grace -> observe -> enforce) with counters and TTLs to avoid stuck states.
- Kernel mapping: add a small table in the runtime that signals whether a profile requires a fallback fused-kernel or will route through optimized paths; flag unknown combinations for canary-only.

Open tradeoffs and considerations:
- Cost vs coverage: Sweeper breadth (many slices/models) increases confidence but costs more GPU time. We'll start with 10 high-risk models and expand.
- Conservative thresholds: We err on false-negatives (keep profile blocked) for initial launches. Later iterations can loosen thresholds based on historical pass rates.

Risks: possible overfitting of sweeper corpora to production distributions; kernel selector changes that shift perf after rollout; unnoticed edge-case for extremely long prefix lengths.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement sweeper and basic runtime hooks in dev environment (this ticket).
2) Internal canary on staging with 2 models (week 1).
3) Broader sweep across 10 models and iterate thresholds (week 2).
4) Promote to runtime-1.22 with opt-in flag for Dedicated customers (week 3).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/display/QI/INT8+Sweeper+Design
- Calibration store schema: drive://redwood/quant/calib-schema.md
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

Next steps: create a prototype sweeper job, wire metrics to metrics-store, add a runtime flag for grace_period, and prepare the staging canary. Assign follow-ups for test-corpus curation and cost estimation.
comments: 2025-03-12 Priya Nair: Created ticket after postmortem for ENG-91456 where an INT8 rollout caused 0.9% perplexity regression for long-prefix requests. Proposed sweeper to reduce manual cycles.

2025-03-13 Ethan Zhao: Spike started. Built initial runner that executes a candidate profile against model-a and collects p50/p95 and token-level logits. Observed that some profiles cause a 15ms p95 jump only on >512 token sequences.
2025-03-14 Design review (L. Morales): Recommend adding 'warmup_tokens' to handle KV-cache heavy models; provided example UX for Console rollout panel.

2025-03-16 Engineering update: Prototype PR opened (link above). Sweeper runs end-to-end on a mini-corpus; cost estimate ~6 GPU-hours per model per full sweep. Added kernel compatibility flags to profile manifests.
2025-03-18 QA note (R. Kim): Added e2e test cases covering fallback during grace and rollback path. Found a flaky case where rollback TTL didn't expire; pushed hotfix branch referencing PR #4330.

2025-03-18 PM alignment (Sara Lane): Agreed to conservative default thresholds: quality_delta_threshold=0.5%, latency_p95_threshold_ms=10. PM requested dashboards to show per-customer impact for Dedicated customers.
notes: Keep initial deployment opt-in for Dedicated and VPC customers. Inform solutions engineering to prepare customer-facing rollout notes.
engineering_runbook: If a rollout triggers quality regression > configured threshold during the grace window: 1) automatically mark profile as failed and route to fallback; 2) create incident doc with sweeper scorecard; 3) notify owners and block auto-promote until manual triage.
test_plan: Unit tests for sweeper parsing and scorecard generation; integration tests for runtime grace state transitions; e2e canary runs against staging models; golden-corpus regression harness runs on every successful sweep.
